text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.97% today as oil prices retreated on hopes for diplomatic progress in the Middle East conflict. Crude had spiked earlier in the week—Brent topped $109 on October 19th after Houthi militants claimed attacks on Saudi facilities—but traders began backing away from those highs on October 20th as optimism about negotiations gained ground. For a refiner like Marathon, lower oil prices compress the margin between what they pay for crude and what they earn selling refined products like gasoline and diesel.

The broader picture shows refining margins under pressure from mixed signals. U.S. refineries are running at 93.5% capacity and gasoline storage is elevated at 208 million barrels, suggesting adequate supply isn't rewarding the refining industry at the moment. The stock is still up 8.5% over two weeks—a reflection of the volatility and the initial crude spike—but today's pullback tracks the market's recalibration as geopolitical risk premiums fade.
